newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia pushes for Bougainville peace.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia pushes for Bougainville peace.

text.p: Australia has stepped up efforts to help broker peace between the Papua New Guinea government and secessionist rebels, offering to fund a plan to bring in international negotiators, Australian sources said on Thursday.

The Australian government, which sponsored failed 1995 peace talks, has offered to fund a private Australian proposal to bring in negotiators to end the nine-year Bougainville conflict, sources familiar with the plan said.
Previously, Canberra had simply offered to help with peace talks if asked by Papua New Guinea and the secessionist Bougainville Revolutionary Army.
Several peace talks and a series of military offensives have failed to end the rebellion.

Australia on Wednesday announced a A$4.0 million aid package to fund medical supplies and health workers after Papua New Guinea agreed to end a ban on aid to the island, 800 km (500 miles) northeast of the capital Port Moresby.

"People are dying on Bougainville, the economy has come to a halt, there is tremendous suffering; we are utterly determined that we do the best we can to help," Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said in Port Moresby on Wednesday.

The Australian newspaper, The Age, on Thursday reported details of the Bougainville peace plan, saying warring factions would be brought together in Australia next month for a conflict resolution course by negotiators from the U.S. Harvard Law School conflict management group.

Under the plan, proposed by two Australian lawyers, the Papua New Guinea government would grant special autonomy to Bougainville and the rebels would accept less than full independence, the newspaper said.
The Australian government would not comment on the plan.
Hundreds of people have died in direct fighting or from disease through a lack of medical supplies during the Bougainville rebellion.
The conflict has also closed the rich Panguna copper mine since May 1989, a major blow to the economy of the impoverished South Pacific nation.
The mine was operated by Bougainville Copper Ltd, a listed subsidiary of RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd.
